title: Annotatio III §.VI open: Two famous post-Reformation Consociation attempts — LIPSIACUM (1631) and CASSELLANUM (1661); the prior distinguished three ways
pass_a_gloss: §. VI. Following the Reformation century, two most famous Efforts of reconciling Protestants among themselves are counted, one the LEIPZIG one, by Saxon, Brandenburg, and Hessian Theologians in the year 1631; the other the CASSEL one, celebrated by Hessian collocutors alone, namely Marburg and Rinteln ones, in the year 1661. The PRIOR is exceedingly distinguished by a threefold title.
pass_b_english: §. VI. After the Reformation century come two most famous Consociation attempts at reconciling Protestants with one another.
One is the Leipzig attempt — Saxon, Brandenburg, and Hessian theologians, 1631; the other the Cassel attempt — Hessian collocutors alone (Marburg and Rinteln), 1661.
The prior (Leipzig) is marked out in three ways.
source_text:
§. VI.
Seculi Reformationem insecuti, Duo famosissima, Protestantes inter se conciliandi, numerantur Molimina, LIPSIACUM unum, Theologis Saxonicis, Brandenburgicis & Hassiaciis An. 1631; alterum CASSELLANUM, ab Hassiaciis solis, Marpurgensibus scilicet & Rintelenfibus, A. 1661, Collocutoribus, celebrata. PRIUS triplici nomine perquam insigne.

lemmas.gloss: the prior under a threefold heading

notes: Hexades Annotatio III §.VI open: LIPSIACUM 1631 + CASSELLANUM 1661 named; PRIUS begins.
